title: Multi-identifier pin resolution guidelines for SDK and API
creator: Aisha Kaplan
description: Problem: Customers can pin models using multiple identifier types (semantic tags, semver ranges, commit hashes) and often combine them across SDK calls and runtime configuration. Current behavior is underspecified leading to surprising runtime fallbacks and cache inconsistencies. This ticket defines deterministic, simple-to-reason-about pin resolution semantics for the Redwood API and SDKs and captures how performance profiles are published and applied when pins resolve to different model artifacts. The goal is stable, auditable resolution order with clear SDK ergonomics and minimal changes to runtime resolver existing code paths.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic resolution precedence is defined and documented for combinations of tag, semver, and commit-hash pins.
SDKs expose a small, consistent surface for pin specification (single field supporting multi-form strings and explicit helpers) and surface telemetry events for resolution results.
Runtime returns explicit resolution metadata in responses (resolved_id, resolution_path, performance_profile_id) and the SDK surfaces this metadata to callers.
Published performance profiles are tied to canonical model artifact refs and applied according to the resolved artifact; tests assert profile selection for each resolution scenario.

Backward compatibility: existing simple exact-tag pins continue to work unchanged; ambiguous pins that previously resolved nondeterministically now follow the documented precedence and produce a non-breaking metadata field.
E2E tests for key scenarios (tag+semver, semver range with prerelease, unknown tag + fallback to latest compatible semver, commit-hash precedence) are green in CI.
design_decisions: Resolution precedence: 1) exact commit hash (full SHA) wins, 2) exact tag name wins, 3) semver range resolves to highest matching semver, 4) 'latest' or empty falls back to runtime default as configured by project. This order minimizes surprise from ephemeral tags while preserving developer expectations for explicit version pins.

Semver handling: support npm-style semver ranges (e.g. ^1.2.0, >=1.0.0 <2.0.0). Pre-release identifiers are excluded unless the requested range explicitly references a pre-release (e.g. 2.0.0-beta.1).
implementation_notes: API: Accept a single 'model' param that can be commit-sha, tag, or semver-range. Add optional query param '?pin=raw' for legacy behavior. Responses include 'x-resolved-model-id' header and 'resolved_model' field in JSON body with canonical id and 'resolution_path' string.

SDK: Provide helpers: Model.pin('v1.2.0'), Model.pinCommit('abc123...'), Model.pinRange('^1.2.0'). Default SDK behavior will call the unified API model resolution endpoint and surface the resolved metadata as ModelResolution object.

Cache invalidation: cache keys must include both the original pin string and the resolved canonical id. When a tag is deleted and re-created, the resolved canonical id changes and caches should miss. Avoid using only tag name as cache key for responses.

Performance profiles: profiles are published against canonical model artifacts (artifact_id), not tag names. When a pin resolves to artifact_id X, the runtime looks up profile X. If no profile exists, runtime falls back to profile for the nearest semver-major compatible artifact or to default profile per deployment tier.

Telemetry: emit 'pin_resolution' event with fields: requested_pin, resolved_type (commit/tag/semver), resolved_artifact, profile_applied, resolution_time_ms. Mark events as high-cardinality for commit hashes and sample them in hosted mode.

Edge cases: if semver range matches multiple artifacts with identical semver (duplicate artifacts), resolve to the artifact with highest build timestamp; surface a warning in metadata. If nothing matches, return 404-like resolution error with suggested candidates in metadata.
test_plan: Unit: resolver unit tests for all precedence permutations (8 permutations covered).

Integration: SDK calls against staging resolver with fixture registry: tags: 'stable', 'canary'; semvers: 1.1.0, 1.2.3, 2.0.0-beta.1; commits mapped to artifacts. Assert response metadata and applied profile id.
E2E: deploy runtime-1.21 with new resolution headers, run sample workload -> ensure correct profile used and perf telemetry aligns with profile expectations.
Cache tests: ensure that after tag re-pointing (tag moved from artifact A to B), cached responses keyed by tag+original-resolved-id become stale and refreshed.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (SDK opt-in): ship SDK helpers and opt-in flag 'pinResolution=explicit' so customers can test resolution metadata without changing existing behavior.
Phase 2 (API header): add 'x-resolved-model-id' header in responses on staging and pair with observability dashboards for pin_resolution events.
Phase 3 (Default): flip runtime to use the new precedence for all requests after one-week opt-in window. Announce breaking-but-deterministic change in developer changelog with examples.
Phase 4 (Profile strictness): after 2 weeks of monitoring, enforce that performance profiles must be published against artifact ids; warn on console when profile missing.
notes: Trade-offs considered: Allowing tag precedence over semver would be friendlier for fast iterative workflows but risked instability when tags get repointed; commit-first protects reproducibility for experiments and production rollouts.
We debated adding a separate 'pin_priority' field in the API but chose unified single-string representation to reduce surface area and encourage consistent pins across SDKs and infra configs.
We will maintain a mapping table in the Console UI that shows tag -> artifact mapping and last change time so operators can audit unexpected resolution shifts.
